name: Topological Star
description: A smooth spacetime of five dimensions with no horizon and no singularity, which seen from four dimensions has the mass and the magnetic charge of a black hole. Where the horizon would be, the circle of the fifth dimension shrinks to a point and space ends on a bubble held open by magnetic flux. Ibrahima Bah and Pierre Heidmann proposed it in 2020 as the simplest topological star, on a line element that also describes a black string with the same bubble behind its horizon.
convention: The radii $r_S$ and $r_B$ are lengths. We keep factors of $c$ explicit.
history: Baltimore, November 2020: Ibrahima Bah and Pierre Heidmann of Johns Hopkins University went looking for a star built from geometry and magnetic flux alone, one that passes for a black hole from far away and has no horizon up close [bah2021]. String theory already had a large number of such objects, the supersymmetric microstate geometries that are the classical fuzzballs of Samir Mathur's proposal, and building one took sophisticated supergravity [bah2021, mathur2005]. What holds them up had become clear in 2013, when Gary Gibbons and Nicholas Warner showed that the mass of a smooth stationary soliton has to come from magnetic flux threading cycles in the topology of space, flux that pushes a cycle open while gravity pulls it shut [gibbons2014fuzzballs, bena2013]. Iosif Bena and Warner gave the idea its name that year, proposing as a possible end point of stellar collapse "Topological Stars, supported by higher-dimensional magnetic fluxes" [bena2013]. Bah and Heidmann wanted the simplest member of the species, and they found it in Einstein's gravity with Maxwell's field in five dimensions [bah2021].¶What does a hole in space look like? One turned up in 1982, when Edward Witten showed that a world with a fifth dimension curled into a circle can decay [witten1982kk, stotyn2011]. The circle shrinks to a point all over a sphere, where space ends, and that bubble of nothing grows until it has eaten the spacetime [witten1982kk, stotyn2011, bah2021]. A bubble that sits still is easy to write down: exchange the time of Schwarzschild's black string with its flat direction, and the horizon becomes the bubble [bah2021]. That bubble has no mass, and it is unstable [bah2021].¶Magnetic flux can hold a bubble open and give it mass [stotyn2011, bah2021]. At the University of Waterloo in 2011, Sean Stotyn and Robert Mann took a black string that carries magnetic charge, exchanged its time with its circle, and obtained "a static magnetically charged soliton", a bubble with mass [stotyn2011]. The string's line element was five years old: Umpei Miyamoto and Hideaki Kudoh had built it from Gary Horowitz and Andrew Strominger's black strings to study when ripples along such a string grow [miyamoto2006, horowitz1991, bah2021]. A circle of a given size allows a small bubble and a large one, Stotyn and Mann found, and the small one survives small disturbances [stotyn2011]. Below a least size of the circle there is no static bubble [stotyn2011].¶Bah and Heidmann wrote the whole family in a line element as short as Schwarzschild's, $$ds^2 = -f_S\,c^2dt^2 + f_B\,dy^2 + \frac{dr^2}{f_Sf_B} + r^2d\Omega^2, \qquad f_S = 1 - \frac{r_S}{r}, \quad f_B = 1 - \frac{r_B}{r},$$ with a magnetic field through each sphere whose strength is fixed by the product $r_Sr_B$ [bah2021]. Time stands still at $r_S$ and the circle $y$ shrinks to a point at $r_B$, and a traveller coming in from far away meets whichever is larger [bah2021]. With $r_S$ the larger, the spacetime is a black string, and exchanging $t$ with $y$ and $r_S$ with $r_B$ turns that string into the star [bah2021]. With $r_B$ the larger, it is the star: space ends on a bubble of radius $r_B$, smoothly, provided the circle far away has the radius $R_y = 2\sqrt{r_B^3/(r_B - r_S)}$ [bah2021]. The plane of $r$ and $y$ is then a cigar: far from the star the circle keeps one girth, and on the way in it narrows until it closes on the bubble like the cigar's tip [bah2021]. From four dimensions the star shows a mass $M = c^2(2r_S + r_B)/(4G)$ and a magnetic charge, the numbers of a black hole [bah2021].¶A smooth bubble can be no wider than the fifth dimension, $2r_B \le R_y$, and a fifth dimension small enough to go unseen makes for a very small star [bah2021]. The name, Bah and Heidmann admitted, "is in that sense too optimistic and should be replaced by 'topological particle'" [bah2021weyl]. Their remedy is to let the tip of the cigar be a cone whose angle is a whole fraction of a full turn, $kR_y = 2\sqrt{r_B^3/(r_B - r_S)}$ for an integer $k$, which is no singularity in string theory, and then $r_B$ can be as large as one likes [bah2021, bah2021weyl]. Given a mass and a charge that a black string also has, the star is twice as wide as the string [bah2021]. Bah, Heidmann, and Peter Weck later built solitons in six dimensions with no net charge, $1.52$ times the size of Schwarzschild's black hole of the same mass [bah2022solitons]. Behind that string's horizon a falling traveller meets the bubble where Schwarzschild's traveller meets a singularity, and the interior, in Bah and Heidmann's words, "caps as a two-dimensional Milne space with a bubble" [bah2021].¶Is the star stable? The first answer was yes for every $r_B > r_S$, on the strength of an analysis by Anindya Dey [bah2021]. Bah, Dey, and Heidmann later narrowed the answer to $r_S < r_B < 2r_S$, the mirror image, under the exchange of time and circle, of the range in which the black string is safe from Ruth Gregory and Raymond Laflamme's instability [bah2022stability, miyamoto2006, gregorylaflamme1993]. Heidmann, Nicholas Speeney, Emanuele Berti, and Bah set a scalar field ringing on the star: for $r_B < 3r_S/2$ light can circle at two radii, one of them on the bubble, and the modes that ring like a black hole's fade more slowly than a black hole's do, held back by the inner of the two [heidmann2023]. Alexandru Dima, Marco Melis, and Paolo Pani found that the most compact stars return waves as echoes [dima2024]. How a star of this kind would form Bah and Heidmann left as "an important open question", and they wondered whether the early universe made such bubbles, small and heavy, "as possible new candidates for dark matter" [bah2021].

related.text: The star's line element with the bubble taken away. At $r_B = 0$ the circle keeps one size everywhere, and the line element is Schwarzschild's black hole at every point of it [bah2021].
At $r_S = 0$ the star is a static bubble of nothing: Schwarzschild's metric with its time made into the circle $y$, and a new time added that feels no gravity [bah2021].
Kaluza and Klein's other smooth magnetic object, whose circle shrinks at a single point. When the tip of the star's bubble is a cone, its two poles carry monopole charges $k$ and $-k$ [bah2021].

The black hole of four dimensions with the same mass and magnetic charge, which Bah and Heidmann set beside the star for comparison. It is no solution of the star's own theory, whose reduction to four dimensions carries a scalar field as well [bah2021].
Milne's universe in two dimensions, a wedge of flat spacetime with its points identified by a boost, is the shape of the black string's interior next to its bubble [bah2021].

Schwarzschild's black hole in more dimensions. Bah and Heidmann build stars in $D + 1$ dimensions by giving Tangherlini's black hole a circle and exchanging that circle with time [bah2021, tangherlini1963].
The same exchange of time and a circle done in anti-de Sitter space, where it needs no flux: the planar black hole's horizon becomes a tip where the circle closes [horowitz1998].

coordinates.name: Bah-Heidmann
domains: r = r_B \;\text{(the bubble, where the circle } y \text{ shrinks to a point)}

parameters.description: Radius at which the horizon of a black string would stand, a length, here inside the bubble; the mass seen from four dimensions is $M = c^2(2r_S + r_B)/(4G)$, with $G$ Newton's constant there
Radius of the bubble, a length, where the circle $y$ shrinks to a point; the square of the magnetic charge is proportional to $r_Sr_B$

coordinates.convention: We use Bah and Heidmann's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi, y)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $y$ a length around the circle of the fifth dimension, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The circle has period $2\pi R_y$ with $R_y = 2\sqrt{r_B^3/(r_B - r_S)}$, which makes the bubble $r = r_B$ a regular point.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r_S\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)}{2r^4}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r\,r_S + r\,r_B - 2r_S\,r_B}{2r\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)}{r}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)\sin^2\theta}{r}\dot{\phi}^2 - \dfrac{r_B\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)}{2r^4}\dot{y}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: About the Bubble
domains: \rho = 0 \;\text{(the bubble, the origin of the plane of } \rho \text{ and } \psi)

parameters.description: Radius at which the horizon of a black string would stand, a length, here inside the bubble; the mass seen from four dimensions is $M = c^2(2r_S + r_B)/(4G)$, with $G$ Newton's constant there
Radius of the bubble, a length, where the circle $\psi$ shrinks to a point; the square of the magnetic charge is proportional to $r_Sr_B$
Bah and Heidmann's radius, a length, the areal radius of the spheres of $\theta$ and $\phi$

coordinates.convention: We use $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi, \psi)$, with Bah and Heidmann's $\rho = 2\sqrt{(r - r_B)/(r_B - r_S)}$, a pure number that vanishes on the bubble, and the angle $\psi = y/R_y$ around the circle of the fifth dimension, $R_y = 2\sqrt{r_B^3/(r_B - r_S)}$. Here $t$ carries dimensions of time, and we take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$.

coordinates.name: Black String, Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein
domains: r = r_B \;\text{(the bubble, where the circle } y \text{ shrinks to a point)}

parameters.description: Radius of the horizon of the black string, a length, here outside the bubble; the mass seen from four dimensions is $M = c^2(2r_S + r_B)/(4G)$, with $G$ Newton's constant there
Radius of the bubble, a length, where the circle $y$ shrinks to a point behind the horizon; the square of the magnetic charge is proportional to $r_Sr_B$

coordinates.convention: We use $(v, r, \theta, \phi, y)$ for the black string, $r_S > r_B$, with the advanced time $v = ct + r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = (1 - r_S/r)^{-1}(1 - r_B/r)^{-1/2}$. The circle $y$ has period $2\pi R_y$ for any length $R_y$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{r_S\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)}{2r^4}\dot{v}^2 - \dfrac{r_S\,\sqrt{r - r_B}}{r^{5/2}}\dot{v}\dot{r} - \dfrac{r_B}{2r\left(r - r_B\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)}{r}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)\sin^2\theta}{r}\dot{\phi}^2 - \dfrac{r_B\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)}{2r^4}\dot{y}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Extremal, Isotropic

parameters.description: The common value of $r_S$ and $r_B$, a length; the mass seen from four dimensions is $M = 3c^2m/(4G)$, with $G$ Newton's constant there

coordinates.convention: We use Bah and Heidmann's isotropic coordinates $(t, \rho, \theta, \phi, y)$ for the extremal black string, $r_S = r_B = m$, with $\rho = r - m$ a length and $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The circle $y$ has period $2\pi R_y$ for any length $R_y$.

coordinates.name: Einstein Metric, Four Dimensions

parameters.description: Radius at which the horizon of a black string would stand, a length; the mass is $M = c^2(2r_S + r_B)/(4G)$
Radius of the bubble of five dimensions, a length; the square of the magnetic charge is proportional to $r_Sr_B$

coordinates.convention: We use $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, Bah and Heidmann's coordinates without the circle, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. The metric is the Einstein metric of four dimensions, the metric of five on a surface of constant $y$ multiplied by $\sqrt{1 - r_B/r}$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(r - r_S\right)\left(2r\,r_S + r\,r_B - 3r_S\,r_B\right)}{4r^4}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r\,r_S + r\,r_B - 3r_S\,r_B}{4r\left(r - r_B\right)\left(r - r_S\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_S\right)\left(4r - 3r_B\right)}{4r}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r - r_S\right)\left(4r - 3r_B\right)\sin^2\theta}{4r}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0
